---
applyTo: "app/**/migrations/**/*.py,alembic.ini"
---

# Database Migrations

SEP has three independent Alembic migration tracks, one per **service** — not one per sub-application. Each track has its own `alembic_version_*` table and own `env.py`. Apps under `app/sep/apps/` get a branch on the `sep` track, never a track of their own.

| Service | Script directory | Version table |
|---|---|---|
| SEP | `app/sep/migrations/` | `alembic_version_sep` |
| Inventory | `app/inventory/migrations/` | `alembic_version_inventory` |
| Tasks | `app/tasks/migrations/` | `alembic_version_tasks` |

## What to check

CI runs `make checkmigrations` on every PR — it catches missing migrations and out-of-date heads automatically. Don't manually flag "model changed but no migration": CI already does. Focus on the manual-judgment items below.

- **Migration lives in the right track, and on the right branch of it.** Within the `sep` track, an app under `app/sep/apps/` that owns a table owns its own branch — its migrations go in `app/sep/apps/<name>/migrations/versions/`, NOT in the shared `app/sep/migrations/versions/`. `alerts`, `atw` and `mysql_backups` work this way today; those dirs are discovered from disk by `discover_plugin_version_dirs` in `app/sep/migrations/_discovery.py` and auto-listed in `[sep] version_locations` by `scripts/sync_alembic_version_locations.py`. The shared track is right only for a migration altering a table the `sep` service itself owns, or one spanning tables owned by two different apps. **The diagnostic:** if landing a table needs an app hardcoded into `_discovery.py`, a second loader path in `env.py`, or the table split into a parallel module because `models.py` is too heavy to import at migration time — the migration is on the wrong branch; relocate it rather than extend the shared registry. Cross-*track* placement (an `app/sep/` model change landing under `app/tasks/migrations/` or `app/inventory/migrations/`) is a hard fail — the migration won't run on the right database.
- **Deleting a sub-app's migration chain is an explicit step.** The sync script refuses to drop an entry already listed in `[sep] version_locations`, because a configured location that is absent from disk or contributes no migration scripts is how the orphan-head filter recognises a stripped app. A deliberate deletion needs `python scripts/sync_alembic_version_locations.py --allow-removals`; anything else (a locally stripped app, a half-deleted package) should restore the directory, or skip the script and run `alembic --name sep upgrade heads` directly — the refusal leaves the entry in place, which is exactly what arms the filter.
- **`upgrade()` and `downgrade()` are both implemented.** Empty `downgrade()` (just `pass`) is a red flag — migrations must be reversible.
- **`downgrade()` reverses `upgrade()`.** New tables in `upgrade()` need `op.drop_table()` in `downgrade()`; new columns need `op.drop_column()`; new indexes need `op.drop_index()`. The pair must be symmetric. A `downgrade()` that re-narrows a column's allowed domain (removes enum members, re-adds `NOT NULL`, shrinks `VARCHAR` length) must first `DELETE`/`UPDATE` rows holding the now-invalid values — otherwise it aborts at runtime the moment such data exists.
- **No data loss without a written strategy.** `op.drop_table()` or `op.drop_column()` on a column that has live data needs an explicit data-migration step (or a justification in the PR description). Same for column type changes that may truncate (`TEXT` → `INTEGER`, `VARCHAR(255)` → `VARCHAR(50)`). A parser branch or deserializer that silently remaps an old stored value at read time is NOT a substitute for a one-shot data migration (`UPDATE`/`DELETE`) — flag it.
- **Column additions on existing tables** must be nullable OR have a server-side default. Non-nullable adds on a populated table will fail at upgrade time. Flag any `op.add_column(..., sa.Column(..., nullable=False))` without a `server_default`. Also flag a new table whose every non-key column is nullable — if a row with nothing populated is meaningless, the migration needs `nullable=False` on at least one required column or a `CheckConstraint`. A backfilled `server_default` must also survive the compatibility window: migrations run ahead of the code rollout, so a release still running the previous code inserts without the column until it restarts — dropping the default in the same migration that adds it breaks the rolling upgrade, and it belongs in a later one.
- **`op.alter_column()` only inside `op.batch_alter_table()`.** SQLite cannot ALTER a column in place, so the bare form is unrunnable there — not merely unidiomatic — and the test suite runs on SQLite. Every existing `alter_column` call site goes through `batch_op`; flag any that doesn't.
- **PostgreSQL-only defects pass the default CI lane.** The main suite runs on SQLite, which silently skips things PostgreSQL enforces, so a migration can be green there and abort on deploy — `add_column` emits an enum's implicit CHECK on PostgreSQL but warns and skips it on SQLite, so a column declared `create_constraint=True` produces the constraint twice on PostgreSQL. SQLite and PostgreSQL are the only engines `DatabaseDialect` carries. **CI is not SQLite-only**, and the second lane is where a dialect-sensitive migration belongs: the `test_postgres` job in `.github/workflows/python.yaml` runs `make test PYTEST_MARKERS='postgres'` against a real `postgres:16-alpine` service (`SEP_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN`), and migration tests already use it — `tests/app/migrations/test_shared_postgres_settingoverride.py` and `tests/app/inventory/migrations/test_mandatory_pmm_origin_postgres.py`. Ask for a `@pytest.mark.postgres` test on the `postgres_engine` / `postgres_session` fixtures. Compiled SQL — `stmt.compile(dialect=postgresql.dialect(), compile_kwargs={"literal_binds": True})` — is supplemental evidence, not a substitute for real-engine execution; when you do read it, read the compiled string rather than the expression tree, since the same Core expression compiles differently depending on how the predicate was composed.
- **A `CONCURRENTLY` index build names its recovery in the module docstring.** A build that fails part-way leaves an INVALID index under the same name, and a re-run matching it with `IF NOT EXISTS` skips it — so the migration reports success on the retry while the index stays invalid, the planner ignores it, and the query it exists for silently falls back to a sequential scan. The docstring must say how to repair it: `REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY <name>`, or drop the index before re-running.
- **Amending an already-applied revision states why, in that file.** A guard, early return, or compatibility branch added to a revision dated months earlier looks inert to the next reader, who has no route from the diff back to the constraint that required it — and a PR description doesn't travel with the file. The reason goes in the `upgrade()` / `downgrade()` docstring, one sentence, at every site that changed. Repeat it per file; don't factor it into a shared constant — each revision is an independent historical record, and a shared constant couples tracks the chain deliberately keeps apart.
- **Index changes are intentional.** Flag unjustified `op.create_index` or `op.drop_index` — they affect production performance. Confirm the index serves a query the diff introduces or removes. Also flag a single-column `op.create_index` / `index=True` on a column already the leading column of a composite index or unique constraint — the composite left-prefix-covers it, so the standalone index only adds write cost.
- **Foreign key constraints** declare `ondelete=` explicitly (`CASCADE`, `SET NULL`, `RESTRICT`). Don't accept FK additions that fall through to the default.
- **Renames are dangerous.** Renaming columns or tables breaks running code during rolling deployment. Flag any `op.alter_column(... new_column_name=...)` or `op.rename_table(...)`. Acceptable only when explicitly coordinated (the PR description names the deployment plan).

## File naming

Generated by Alembic from the configured template; format is `%%(year)d_%%(month).2d_%%(day).2d_%%(hour).2d%%(minute).2d-%%(rev)s_%%(slug)s` (Alembic appends `.py`; the resolved filename ends `…%%(slug)s.py`). Flag manually-written filenames that don't match (timestamp prefix is load-bearing — it orders the migration history).

## env.py expectations

Each track's `env.py` imports its own models and settings, uses `async_engine_from_config`, and points `target_metadata` at `SQLModel.metadata`. Don't accept diffs that point one track's `env.py` at another track's models or metadata. Each `env.py` also imports `compare_type` from `app/core/db/utils` and passes it to the `run_migrations_*` calls — don't accept a diff that drops or replaces it. A cross-package model imported **solely** to register with `SQLModel.metadata` belongs in `env.py`, not in a service `models.py` with `# noqa: F401`; flag such a registration-only import in a `models.py`.
